## Design

### 2026-10-06 – KiCAD looking pretty cool

**1h**

KiCAD looking pretty cool
2:20 AM to 3:22 AM

To actually start my project, I have to figure out what I need to make it work, so I did research into the components I would need and ended up with the following:
ESP32
LCD Display
3x Buttons
1x Potentiometer

With those locked down, I got to work on KiCAD making the schematic. This was my first time using KiCAD or working on a PCB, so I used the Starbie guide to help me get started and just changed it to suit my project.

I started by adding the component for the ESP32, the same as the Starbie one, to the schematic. This took me a bit to figure out because I needed to download the .sym files from the Starbie care package.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 025122](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/d13d523e31ec3bf6c607397b8a0bbfaaa1415c64c0544ac61862ee543a8657d8.png)

I ended up getting it into the schematic and adding the labels and symbols for power, ground, and the GPIOs. Then I started looking at the screen and what I would need for that. The screen that I'm using is different from the Starbie screen, so I put in a 01x08 connector for it and made the net labels for everything that it needs to connect to on the ESP32 after looking into the ports and connections. I also put in the three buttons that I need, which was pretty simple as its just the GPIOs and ground.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 032033](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/e6430c56c15a923d0b7385e78febe54676595a91275d36c71d0d542e94a4db07.png)

I still need to add the potentiometer for the volume control but it's looking good so far and I ended up getting the hang of KiCAD and schematics pretty quickly.

As of writing this I have not updated the BOM but I will do so immediately. Pretty much everything is still technically up for debate as to whether I'm actually using it or a different model, but I think I should be sticking with them.

tl;dr: Started work on the schematic for the PCB layout.

### 2026-10-07 – PCB has been designed!

**2.5h**

PCB has been designed!
10:37 PM to 1:10AM

After figuring out KiCAD using the starbie guide yesterday, I wrapped up the schematic by adding the potentiometer that I found online. That was the last of the components needed.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 231320](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/93470ee324e467aa33ceac0a73f3e00be64b7c415cd481377918b81bfaa57ca2.png)

With the schematic done, I assigned the footprints to each component. For the ESP32 and the switches I  used the same ones as the starbie guide, but for the screen and potentiometer I had to figure out what to use. Eventually I did research and got a 2.54mm pinheader for the screen and a alps potentiometer.

After the footprints were done, I double checked my schematic to make sure I wasn't missing anything and then switched over to the PCB editor. I dropped in everything from the schematics and organized it to look nice. I made a simple rectangular outline with rounded edges for the PCB and played around with some of the component orientations to get a layout that worked for routing connections.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 001423](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/f95b87b6265d0049be997a8e173636dc4171d451f19772f72e81cc14b1cf5dbc.png)

The PCB was looking pretty good, but I realized that I should make the routes for the 3.3V power larger so I turned them into 6mm instead of 2mm. Then I had to figure out how to do the ground fill, but I got it in pretty easily and everything looked to be good. The DRC also came back good with 0 issues, so I exported the gerber and drill files and uploaded them to the repo.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 012409](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/b7118fde471955549a03de9d428efe9bbe826e84a07d9b013109c1297d496a03.png)

Next time I work on this I'm going to put the PCB into JLCPCB as well as start working on firmware for the project.

tl;dr: Finished PCB layout, need to start on firmware.

### 2026-10-11 – Almost had a really big problem, but CAD fixed it

**3h**

Almost had a really big problem, but CAD fixed it
10:23 AM - 1:28 PM

To take a break from the firmware coding, I started on a simple stand for this PCB. I want it on my table standing up so the screen is easy to view, but I don't necessarily need anything to cover the PCB. I opened Onshape and put in the step file from KiCAD and started finding and importing models for all the components, which is when I realized that the potentiometer that I'm using is incorrect from the one in KiCAD. I used a standard potentiometer footprint that has 2.56mm hole spacing, but the one that I was going to buy had 5mm hole spacing. Needless to say, this is a pretty big issue but its a good thing I caught it. I spent a long time trying to see if I can find a footprint for the 5mm hole spacing, but I was unable to do so. Instead of making my own footprint, I figured why not just swap the potentiometers. I found one on amazon that had the 2.56mm hole spacing, so I just updated my KiCAD layout to be more accurate and went with that.

This is what the new layout is:

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 131612](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/d5113744a7be5b9f567aabadc5ede1b07ca2c2fa8543b52c85739cf10267029e.png)

This is what the CAD for the board looks like:
![Screenshot 2026-10-11 132349](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/8ff938d70f5c4d3fab5845177f8ed79c2641ffead88cc3f132b463f8859d4f63.png)

The new layout had no issues in both the DRC and the JLC quote maker, so with that done I started on the stand for it. Its pretty basic, I didn't want to cover the PCB, just to support it, so it's basically just an angled block, but I think it looks pretty cool.
![Screenshot 2026-10-11 132358](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/cVf1AKGAA4bfEud82NdRBGOmHvDBJZX3/590edd26ac0777d524dd7a8190f082227fe20b28cf7738c432d22c2105626f1a.png)

I uploaded the CAD to the repo and updated all the KiCAD files with the new layout, now I got to go back to working on firmware.
